blocks.text: Have you ever wondered how mathematicians group objects together? This is where the concept of sets comes in handy!

blocks.markdown: A **set** is a collection of distinct objects, considered as an object in its own right. Sets are fundamental objects in mathematics.

blocks.title: Definition of a Set
blocks.text: A set is a well-defined collection of distinct objects, such as numbers, people, or letters.

blocks.markdown: Sets can be described in two main ways: **roster notation** and **set-builder notation**. In roster notation, we list all elements of the set, e.g., $A = \{1, 2, 3\}$. In set-builder notation, we define a set by a property that its members must satisfy, e.g., $B = \{x | x > 0\}$.

blocks.title: Identifying Subsets
blocks.prompt: Identify if set $C = \{2, 4\}$ is a subset of set $D = \{1, 2, 3, 4, 5\}$.

steps.text: List all elements of set $C$ and set $D$.
Check if every element of $C$ is also an element of $D$.
Since 2 and 4 are in $D$, $C$ is a subset of $D$.

blocks.markdown: The **universal set** is the set that contains all objects under consideration, often denoted by $U$. The **empty set**, denoted by $\emptyset$, is the set containing no elements.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: Remember, the empty set is a subset of every set, including itself!

blocks.markdown: The **union** of two sets $A$ and $B$, denoted $A \cup B$, is the set of elements that are in $A$, in $B$, or in both. The **intersection** of two sets $A$ and $B$, denoted $A \cap B$, is the set of elements that are in both $A$ and $B$. The **complement** of a set $A$, denoted $A'$, is the set of elements in the universal set $U$ that are not in $A$.

points: A set is a collection of distinct objects.
Sets can be described using roster or set-builder notation.
Subsets, universal sets, and empty sets are key concepts in set theory.
Union, intersection, and complement are operations on sets.
